slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on API
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **API**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,

• Define what an **API** is.
• Explain the role of an **API** key.
• Identify the components of an **API** request.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Prerequisites

slides.title: What is an API?
slides.narration:
What is an **API**?
An **API**, or **Application Programming Interface**, acts as a messenger.
It connects your application to a model.
Imagine an **API** as a restaurant waiter.
You give your order, a request, to the waiter.
The waiter takes it to the kitchen, the model.
Then, the waiter brings your dish, the response, back to you.
This is how an **API** helps applications communicate.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a restaurant waiter connecting a customer (application) to a kitchen (model).

slides.title: What is an API Key?
slides.narration:
But how does the **API** know who you are?
This is where an **API** key helps.
An **API** key is a unique, secret password.
It identifies you as an authorized user.
Think of it like an ID card at a restaurant.
It proves you are allowed to place an order.
This key ensures only authorized users access the service.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of an ID card or a secret key for authentication.

slides.title: Understanding an API Request
slides.narration:
With an **API** and an **API** key, you can make a request.
An **API** request is how you talk to the **AI** model.
It's like telling the chef exactly what you want.
Your request always includes your **API** key.
This key authenticates you as an authorized user.
Then, you add your specific **prompt** or instruction.
For example, 'Write a poem about a cat'.
The **API** delivers this entire request to the model.
The model processes it and gives you a response.
slides.image_prompt: Person at laptop, showing elements of an API request with an API key and a prompt.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined **APIs** as messengers between applications and models.
We understood **API** keys are for identification and authentication.
Finally, we explored **API** requests as the way to interact with **AI** models.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Identify daily applications that use **APIs**.
Think about how they send and receive information.
Compare the results.
